newsitem.title: ITALY: Cuba's Castro dines with Italy's Agnelli.
newsitem.headline: Cuba's Castro dines with Italy's Agnelli.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro went to dinner on Sunday with Italy's most famous businessman, Gianni Agnelli, the honorary chairman of carmaker Fiat SpA, witnesses said.

Castro's huge security escort of Italian police and Cuban guards waited outside Agnelli's Rome residence. A police officer at the scene said the 70-year-old revolutionary was inside the imposing building, opposite Italy's presidential palace.
The Italian news agency ANSA said Castro was dining with Agnelli and his sister, former Italian foreign minister Susanna Agnelli. No Fiat officials were present, it said.
Fiat is Italy's largest private sector company, with more than 1,000 holdings. The Agnelli family controls about one third of the company's stock.
Castro arrived in Italy on Saturday to attend a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit which ended on Sunday and is due to have an historic audience with Pope John Paul at the Vatican on Tuesday.

Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi urged Castro at talks on Saturday to demonstrate "real change in the human rights situation" in Cuba, especially concerning political and civil freedoms, according to Prodi's office.
The statement added that Prodi and Castro both hoped to develop economic and commercial links between Italy and Cuba. The Caribbean island has been under a U.S. embargo for 34 years.
